title: Stratified probe fence and rollout inspector for prompt-set linked regression detection
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Problem: We currently detect behavioral regressions using a mix of ad-hoc probe queries and per-customer heuristics. This has led to noisy alerts and slow detection of subtle quality degradation during staged deployments (shadow, A/B, canaries). There is insufficient stratification across prompt cohorts (short/long, code/QA, instruction vs conversational) and we lack an inspector that correlates population-level metric shifts with specific probe cohorts and model change fingerprints.

Proposal: Build a Stratified Probe Fence and Rollout Inspector: a lightweight, reproducible pipeline that runs a curated set of canonical probe cohorts (canonical probes = representative prompts grouped by semantic cohort) against candidate model variants during shadow and canary phases, computes cohort-level metrics plus divergence fingerprints, and surfaces cohort-weighted alarms and an explainable regression report in the Console. The inspector will: 1) support stratified sampling of probes (cohort-aware sampling, per-customer anchors), 2) compute multiple metrics (BLEU-like, semantic-similarity via embeddings, hallucination heuristics, token-level latency/failure rates), 3) produce a fingerprint diff (top divergent prompts + contributing tokens), and 4) feed a decision engine that can (a) auto-quarantine a rollout when high-confidence cohort regressions occur, (b) flag human review with suggested remediation, or (c) escalate to auto-rollback depending on severity and policy.

Design highlights and trade-offs: 
- Probe composition: we will maintain probe cohorts as versioned artifacts in the eval-store (small JSONL bundles). Each probe has metadata: cohort, expected behavior tags, sensitivity weight. Avoid an enormous golden set — use stratified, small, high-signal probes to minimize noise and runtime cost.
- Metrics: prefer a composite metric mixing semantic similarity (embedding distance), scalar heuristics (toxicity/hallucination flags), and agreement with reference outputs where available. Composite thresholds are tuned per-cohort.
- Sampling and traffic modes: inspector runs in two modes: shadow (runs all probes on candidate and baseline, asynchronous) and canary (samples live traffic requests, replays prefix contexts where consent allows). For privacy, live replay uses hashed prompt fingerprints and does not store raw customer text unless opt-in.
- Thresholding & decision engine: implement a probabilistic scoring model that accounts for cohort size, metric variance, and prior release history. Auto-quarantine triggers require both a high cohort-weighted score and a secondary human-approved checklist for high customer impact cohorts.
- Performance: inspector runs are batched against runtime endpoints. We will instrument KV cache warm-up and ensure batch sizes do not violate latency SLOs for production traffic. For dedicated/private customers, agent will support local execution of the probe-runner to avoid egress.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to merge):
- Probe registry: API to register, version, and query probe cohorts; store artifact links (confluence/design doc + JSONL).
- Runner: a repeatable job that runs N probe cohorts against baseline and candidate variants, produces cohort metrics and fingerprint diffs.
- Console integration: an inspector UI card that shows cohort-level deltas, top 10 divergent probes with diffs, and an action panel (quarantine, mark-noise, request human review).
- Automated policy: pluggable policy config per-customer that maps composite score thresholds to actions (alert, quarantine, rollback).
- Tests: unit tests for metric computation, integration test that simulates staged rollout (shadow -> canary -> abort) and verifies the decision engine responds correctly.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Stratified+Probe+Fence+Design
- Implementation spec (internal doc): https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ProbeFenceSpec
- Example PR (implementation WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2389

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement probe registry + small proof-of-concept runner against hosted dev endpoints (non-prod).
- Week 2: instrument metrics and fingerprint diff logic; wire to a lightweight console mock.
- Week 3: policy rules + integration tests; run controlled shadow experiments for two customers and internal staging.
- Week 4: graduate to canary with auto-quarantine enabled for low-risk cohorts; human-in-the-loop for high-impact cohorts.

Operational notes: probe artifacts should be small (<= 5k probes total per release) to keep compute cost bounded. We will cache embeddings for static probes to reduce compute. For private deployments, provide a local runner binary and a minimal report uploader that sends only aggregated diffs for central indexing.

Security & privacy: live prompt replay is restricted by policy; default is hash-only. Any storage of customer prompts requires opt-in and an audit trail (KMS-encrypted).

Open questions:
- How to set cohort sensitivity weights objectively? Proposed approach: calibrate weights using historical regression events and customer-reported incidents.
- What is the minimum probe set for each model family? Start with 100-300 high-signal probes per family and iterate.

Success criteria (post-release):
- Time-to-detection of quality regressions in staged rollouts reduced by 50% compared to existing ad-hoc alerts.
- False-positive quarantine rate < 3% on internal canaries.
- Console adoption: product teams enable inspector for >= 50% of new model rollouts within 6 weeks.
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — registry API schema drafted and a proof-of-concept JSONL probe bundle created. Verified embedding caching reduces repeated compute by ~40% in dev.

2026-03-04: Architecture review with PM & Observability: decided to limit default probe-run to 200 probes per run and prioritize cohort-aware weighting. PM asked for clear exportable report for CS teams.

2026-03-06: Implemented runner skeleton + metric functions. Discovered discrepancy between embedding similarity libraries across runtime and eval harness; added a compatibility shim to normalize vectors.
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff: confirmed live-replay will be opt-in and hashed-by-default. Need follow-up ticket for KMS audit trail for any stored customer prompts.
Next steps: finish console visualization prototype, finalize auto-quarantine policy DSL, begin integration tests with staging canary pipeline.
